title: Gardenio — Cost X-Check Trust (double-check principle)

options.content: **The double-check.** Every important quantity is measured two independent ways; `gardenio_xcheck_agreement` is the ratio between those two derivations per pair, so **1.0 means the two reconstruct each other** and a persistent dip means one side is wrong — the instrumentation, the assumption, or the mental model. Read agreement first, then the trailing-6h view the `CostXCheckDrift` alert fires on, then side A vs side B for the pair that drifted. A cost number on another board is only as trustworthy as its pair here.

panels.title: Corroboration headline — gardenio_xcheck_agreement per pair (C5 ka-0000006644)
Pairs drifting below 0.95 (now)
panels.description:
How many conservation pairs currently score below the CostXCheckDrift default floor (0.95). Each pair is the same quantity derived from two independent sources; agreement = 1 − |A−B| / max(A,B,ε). Non-zero here for 6h files a CostXCheckDrift ticket.

`< bool 0.95` scores every REPORTED pair 0/1 and sums, so a healthy board reads a measured 0 (we saw the pairs and none drifted) while a gauge that stops reporting reads empty and falls through to the noValue. The previous `count(... < 0.95) or vector(0)` rendered both cases as an identical confident green 0 (ka-0000006531).

defaults.noValue: gardenio_xcheck_agreement not reporting — drift count UNKNOWN (not 0)

panels.title: Agreement by pair (now)
panels.description: Current corroboration score per pair. 100% = the two independent derivations agree exactly. Pairs: bill-conservation (P1 Σ/key/info vs attributed+unattributed), tag-conservation (P2 role vs project vs model tag sums), sessions-vs-agent (P4 session settled vs agent LiteLLM delta), rollup-vs-tree (P5 gardener rollup vs live BFS), token-parity (P6 coop-scraped vs gb-pushed tokens), interrupt-parity (P9 deaths counter vs bead scan), agent-spend-parity (P10 old stateful settle vs new stateless /spend/logs recompute). P3 settled-vs-bill was retired (ka-0000000543) — its at-close counter went dead; P1 + P10 cover its ground. P7 estimate-vs-settled was retired (ka-0000007296) — its in-pod estimate lost its producer when coop went cost-free.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_xcheck_agreement series for $env / $pair — the cross-check job has not published an agreement ratio, so corroboration is UNKNOWN, not perfect. Clear the $pair filter first; if still empty the cross-check is not running.

panels.title: Agreement per pair over time (→ 1.0 = corroborated)
panels.description: The 'graph correctness improvement' trend: each line is one conservation pair's corroboration score. As cost-pipeline fixes land, lines should climb toward 1.0 and stay there; a line sagging below the red 0.95 floor for 6h fires CostXCheckDrift. A line that VANISHES is a pair whose sweep could not derive both sides this cycle (source down / scan truncated) — absence is deliberate honesty, never a fabricated score.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_xcheck_agreement series for $env / $pair in this range — nothing was published in the window, so agreement is UNKNOWN. Empty must never be read as agreement: a corroborated pair draws a line at 1.0.

panels.title: Alert view — what CostXCheckDrift fires on
Trailing-6h max agreement per pair (below the line = alert firing)
panels.description: max_over_time(agreement[6h]) — the exact `for: 6h` semantics of CostXCheckDrift: a pair only drops below the red 0.95 line here once its agreement has been below the floor CONTINUOUSLY for six hours, i.e. exactly when the alert transitions to firing. A raw-agreement dip that recovers within the window never pulls this curve down.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_xcheck_agreement samples in the trailing 6h for $env / $pair — CostXCheckDrift has nothing to evaluate, so the alert is BLIND rather than quiet. Treat empty as an unmonitored window.

panels.title: Settlement health — the direct diagnostic (no grade-audit run needed)
Unsettled sessions backlog (gardenio_unsettled_sessions)
panels.description: The settlement-sweep backlog: closed agent beads still awaiting cost settlement (spend_settlement_sweep.go). This is the DIRECT settlement-pipeline diagnostic — surfaced here (ka-0000000543) so a settlement collapse is visible on the trust board rather than only inside a grade-audit run. Healthy shape is a sawtooth that repeatedly drains to 0 as each sweep clears its queue; a sustained non-zero floor or a monotonic climb is a real stuck backlog (settle failures, lost baselines, or the sweep not running). Retired pair P3 settled-vs-bill used to be the (structurally-broken) proxy for this — this gauge is the honest replacement.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_unsettled_sessions series for $env — the settlement exporter is not reporting, so the backlog is UNKNOWN, not drained. A live exporter with a clean backlog draws a flat 0 line.

panels.title: Side A vs side B — the two independent derivations, per pair
Side A vs side B — $pair
panels.description: Both raw sides of the pair overlaid, so a low agreement score is immediately attributable: which derivation moved, and when. Units are per-pair (USD for the bill/settlement pairs, tokens for token-parity, deaths for interrupt-parity) — compare the two lines against each other, not across panels. Gaps mean the sweep could not derive both sides that cycle and deliberately published nothing.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_xcheck_value series for $env / pair="$pair" — neither independent derivation was published, so there is nothing to reconcile. Pick a different $pair; if every pair is empty the cross-check job is not running.

panels.title: Agreement distribution across pairs — p05 / p50 / p95
panels.description: Quantiles of agreement taken across all cross-check pairs at each instant. p05 is the worst-corroborated pair in the fleet: if it sits below 0.95 while p50 stays at 1.0, exactly one derivation is broken and the bargauge above names it.

panels.description: One row per cross-check pair: current agreement plus the two raw values it is the ratio of. This is where you see *which* side moved, without switching the $pair variable.

description: The cost double-check: per-pair agreement between two independently-derived measurements of the same quantity (1.0 = the two derivations reconstruct each other), the trailing-6h view the CostXCheckDrift alert fires on, settlement backlog, and the raw side-A vs side-B series. Open this before trusting any cost number on another board.
